The angular size of the event horizon is given as \(\theta = 10^{-17}\) degrees at a distance \(d = 10^{10}\) parsecs. Converting to radians: \(\theta_{\text{rad}} = 10^{-17} \times \frac{\pi}{180} \approx 1.745 \times 10^{-19}\) rad.  
Distance in meters: \(d = 10^{10} \times 3.086 \times 10^{16} \approx 3.086 \times 10^{26}\) m.  
Assuming the angular size refers to the angular diameter, the Schwarzschild radius is \(R_s = \frac{d \cdot \theta_{\text{rad}}}{2} \approx 2.69 \times 10^7\) m.  
The entropy of a black hole is given by the Bekenstein-Hawking formula:  
\(S = \frac{k_B A}{4 l_P^2} = \frac{k_B \cdot 4\pi R_s^2}{4 l_P^2} = k_B \pi \left(\frac{R_s}{l_P}\right)^2\).  
Using Planck length \(l_P \approx 1.616 \times 10^{-35}\) m and Boltzmann constant \(k_B \approx 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\) J/K:  
\(\frac{R_s}{l_P} \approx 1.66 \times 10^{42}\), so \(\left(\frac{R_s}{l_P}\right)^2 \approx 2.76 \times 10^{84}\).  
\(S \approx 1.38 \times 10^{-23} \times \pi \times 2.76 \times 10^{84} \approx 1.2 \times 10^{62}\) J/K.  
The order of magnitude is \(10^{62}\) J/K.

Answer: A
